summary: Cloudflare Workers environment prevents dynamic code generation from strings required by the Temporal TypeScript client during protobuf initialization, causing connection failures. User worked around it by implementing manual gRPC protocol communication.
userImpact: Users cannot use the Temporal TypeScript client from Cloudflare Workers due to environment restrictions on dynamic code generation, forcing them to implement low-level gRPC calls as a workaround.
rootCause: Cloudflare Workers environment disallows code generation from strings (EvalError), which is triggered by protobufjs during client initialization. The underlying issue stems from protobufjs/protobuf.js#1754 and dynamic require() calls in data-converter-helpers.js.
proposedFix: Update @temporalio/common to avoid dynamic require() in data-converter-helpers.js when running in restricted environments, or provide a Cloudflare Workers-compatible configuration option.
workaround: Implement raw gRPC protocol communication using temporal.api.workflowservice.v1 protobuf messages and fetch API, manually framing the protobuf messages according to gRPC wire protocol.
resolutionDetails: Issue was closed as the problem stems from Cloudflare Workers environment restrictions rather than an SDK bug. User found a workaround by bypassing the client library and using raw gRPC calls.
keyQuote: This code should run on the 'server side', I just need to cancel a running workflow (I try to find a rest api but I think temporal does not expose it)
